findings.statement: CA9 is up-regulated in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712) and persists at purity 1 (7.787), so it is tumour-cell intrinsic; girentuximab reached PHASE_3. It is not prognostic (Cox log HR -0.009).

SCARB1 ranks first in the target profile: RNA log2FC 2.974, protein log2FC 1.837, TCGA log2FC 3.989 and a purity-1 RNA log2FC of 3.762 (SE 0.408), indicating tumour-intrinsic overexpression. It has no ccRCC dependency signal (DepMap mean effect 0.002) and no drugs.

CD70 is up-regulated at RNA (log2FC 4.464) and protein (log2FC 2.421), replicates in TCGA (log2FC 7.09) and keeps a purity-1 RNA log2FC of 4.278. It is a membrane ligand with clinical-stage antibodies (cusatuzumab PHASE_2, vorsetuzumab mafodotin PHASE_1).

ENPP3 is up at RNA (log2FC 3.895) and protein (log2FC 1.544), replicates in TCGA (log2FC 5.557) and has a purity-1 RNA log2FC of 5.278. It has a 18.2% copy-number loss rate (cnv_loss_freq 0.182) and an ADC (AGS-16C3F, PHASE_2).

SLC16A3 (a lactate transporter) is up at RNA (log2FC 3.435) and protein (log2FC 2.279), replicates in TCGA (log2FC 3.291) with a purity-1 RNA log2FC of 3.821, and shows a positive cis copy-number effect (rho 0.258). It is undrugged and not prognostic at BH<0.05 (Cox padj 0.0887).

NNMT is strongly up at RNA (log2FC 4.67) and protein (log2FC 2.709), replicates in TCGA (log2FC 4.685) and high expression is associated with worse survival (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479), giving the top biomarker-profile score among up-regulated genes. DepMap mean effect in ccRCC is 0.316, so a dependency is not supported.

FABP6 is up at RNA (log2FC 4.006) and protein (log2FC 1.921) and replicates in TCGA (log2FC 6.431). It shows frequent copy-number gain (cnv_gain_freq 0.573) with a positive cis effect (rho 0.309), so gain is a plausible dosage driver.

PSAT1 is down in tumour at RNA (log2FC -3.867) and protein (log2FC -1.963), replicates in TCGA (log2FC -2.974) and low expression predicts worse survival (Cox log HR 0.43, padj 5.66e-7). It is the top biomarker-profile gene.

ALDH6A1, a loss-of-tubule-identity marker, is down at RNA (log2FC -3.399) and protein (log2FC -1.925), with 0.355 copy-number loss frequency and a strong positive cis effect (rho 0.525). Low expression is associated with worse survival (Cox log HR -0.554, padj 9.45e-12), but the purity-1 RNA log2FC shrinks to -1.973.

VWF is up at RNA (log2FC 3.605) and protein (log2FC 1.284) and is associated with better survival (Cox log HR -0.397, padj 1.97e-7). It is an endothelial/vascular signal and its tumour-cell origin is less certain (purity-1 RNA log2FC 3.521), making it a biomarker rather than a tumour-cell target despite approved vWF-directed drugs.

L1CAM is down in tumour at RNA (log2FC -2.623) and protein (log2FC -1.714), replicates in TCGA (log2FC -5.785) and low expression is associated with worse survival (Cox log HR 0.328, padj 0.00000567); its loss is a biomarker, not a target.

PCK1 is down at RNA (log2FC -4.424) and protein (log2FC -1.859), reflecting loss of proximal-tubule gluconeogenic identity, replicates in TCGA (log2FC -3.079) and is associated with worse survival when low (Cox log HR -0.415, padj 1.91e-7).
VHL is somatically mutated in 247 of 511 ccRCC tumours (frequency 0.483, padj 0.0), the dominant driver behind the HIF-driven up-regulation of CA9, ANGPTL4 and related genes.
PBRM1 is mutated in 185 of 511 tumours (frequency 0.362, padj 4.59e-239) and lies on 3p with a copy-number loss frequency of 0.8 in CPTAC, consistent with the two-hit 3p loss plus mutation mechanism.

caveats: Dependency (DepMap) evidence is weak for the top up-regulated genes (mean ccRCC effects near zero or positive except SCD, -0.501), so target claims rest on expression, replication and tractability, not essentiality.
Bulk tumour comparisons can include stromal/endothelial contributions (e.g. VWF); purity-1 extrapolations have wide SEs.
Protein log2FC values are TMT ratios and are compressed relative to RNA log2FC.
Safety in normal tissue was not assessed by the omics layers; prognosis is from univariate Cox in TCGA-KIRC only.
Not all ranked genes had individual calls to rna_protein_correlation; values come from the convergence ranking rows and per-gene DE queries.

findings.statement: CA9 is the top-ranked convergent gene and the literature agrees with the omics (tumour-up). PMID:42473996 reports CA9 is preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumor cells with low background expression in normal kidney tissue. PMID:42205867 calls CA9 a promising target for site-specific drug delivery. Evidence is mostly imaging/delivery proof-of-concept, not a validated clinical biomarker in this corpus.

PMID:42473996: CA9-targeted PET gives proof-of-concept evidence for noninvasive discrimination of ccRCC, 'warranting prospective validation'; high uptake is associated with PBRM1 loss-of-function alterations. A single early study; prospective validation is still pending. The Ndufa4l2 paper (PMID:34970493) links Ndufa4l2 to Ca9 expression in a mouse early-ccRCC model (mechanism).

CD70 is described as commonly overexpressed in RCC and minimally expressed in normal tissue, making it a potential therapeutic target (PMID:38195301); PMID:39510586 says its high and specific ccRCC expression makes it a potential diagnostic and therapeutic target. Omics (tumour-up, purity-robust) and tractability (antibody drugs in the ranking) are concordant. Literature is preclinical/early-clinical in this corpus.

PMID:38195301: CD70 expression correlates with hypoxia pathway proteins in ccRCC, consistent with CD70 being a downstream HIF target. PMID:39510586 developed 68Ga-labelled CD70-specific single-domain antibodies (RCCB3, RCCB6) as radiotracers, and reports CD70 expression associated with overall survival of RCC patients (direction not stated in the sentence).

NNMT is upregulated in ccRCC tumour tissue and high expression correlated with worse overall and disease-specific survival (PMID:41399267), which matches the TCGA Cox signal in the ranking. The authors call it a promising prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target. Selective NNMT inhibitors (II559, II802) exist with >5000-fold selectivity (PMID:37523719, general chemistry paper), but no clinical drug is listed. NNMT is also the best biomarker-profile gene in the top set. Single retrospective study.

ALDOB is downregulated in ccRCC (IHC notably diminished versus adjacent normal tissue, PMID:40852386) and proposed as prognostic biomarker and potential immunotherapy target; PMID:38655323 calls it an independent predictor of prognosis in KIRC. Associated with infiltrating Treg, Th17 cells and neutrophils. Both are bioinformatic plus limited IHC studies; a lost-expression gene is a poor direct drug target, consistent with the data-only target profile being low.

Contradictory directionality: MT1G is downregulated in ccRCC versus normal kidney (PMID:36204178; PMID:38906969), yet high MT1G correlates with advanced stage and poorer prognosis, and elevated MT1G promoted growth and metastasis in vitro and in vivo. Mechanisms: MT1G inhibits CPT1B via H3K14 trimethylation to enhance lipid droplet accumulation; it is a negative regulator of ferroptosis; SAP30 inhibits MT1G transcription and thus p53 zinc delivery (PMID:40247376). Biomarker use needs care because the tumour-vs-normal and prognostic directions differ.

ABAT is significantly underexpressed in KIRC among 11 cancers and predicted poor prognosis in KIRC (pan-cancer analysis, PMID:41158242, bioinformatic). Mechanistic work (PMID:41813748) shows ABAT overexpression suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in vivo, mediating cGAS-STING and interacting with PRMT5 to enhance interferon signaling. Tumour-suppressor-like; the tumour type of the functional work is not stated in the returned sentences. Vigabatrin is listed as a drug in the ranking, but no ccRCC therapeutic literature was found.

SLC22A8 protein, phosphorylated protein and DNA methylation levels were lower in ccRCC than normal tissue, low methylation predicted poor overall survival, and it 'can be used as a prognostic biomarker' (PMID:36123895). Single bioinformatic-plus-validation report; omics and TCGA survival are concordant (down in tumour, favourable-with-high-expression).

UMOD downregulation in ccRCC is reproduced across independent studies (PMID:36899967 methylation/expression clusters; PMID:37275334 validation; PMID:35795483 in HIV-associated kidney cancer). It is a robust tumour-vs-normal marker of lost nephron differentiation, but no prognostic or therapeutic claim is made, and TCGA Cox is not significant in the ranking.

PMID:42769428: promoter hypermethylation is associated with NPHS2 downregulation in ccRCC; NPHS2 overexpression suppressed malignant behaviour, attenuated EMT and weakened immune evasion in vitro, and NPHS2 loss may reduce sunitinib sensitivity. Single preprint-like study, in vitro, hypothesis-level.

The FABP1 literature relations in this corpus concern colorectal and lung adenocarcinoma (PMID:35951102: reduced expression in colorectal cancer; IHC helps identify metastatic colorectal/GI adenocarcinoma to the lung), not ccRCC. The omics/TCGA support for FABP1 in ccRCC is therefore not corroborated by ccRCC-specific literature here.

SCARB1 (rank 5, target-profile score highest in the top 12, tumour-up and purity-robust, Open Targets genetic association) and PIGR (rank 6) have no literature relations in the corpus (only Open Targets association records); searches returned only generic ccRCC sentences. These are data-supported candidates with essentially no corpus literature, i.e. potentially novel.

caveats: Only the top 12 of the convergence ranking were examined in detail; ranks 13-40 were not reviewed.

Most gene-level claims come from single bioinformatic (TCGA-based) or small IHC studies; only CA9 and CD70 have imaging/targeting translational work, and these are early (proof-of-concept, radiotracer, delivery).
MT1G has an apparent contradiction: downregulated in tumour but high expression associated with poor prognosis and tumour promotion.
FABP1 literature is not about ccRCC; SCARB1 and PIGR have no literature relations; ABAT functional evidence may derive from non-ccRCC models.

gene_scores was not queried separately; profile scores were taken from the convergence_ranking rows. Down-regulated genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1, NPHS2, MT1G, ABAT) score high as biomarkers but low as targets in the data-only profile, so literature 'potential target' claims for them are not supported by the data.
DepMap dependency is near zero for CA9, so CA9 is a delivery/imaging target (antibody, PET) rather than a functional dependency.

findings.statement: CA9 is rank 1 in convergence (score 4.5197, 5 streams). TCGA tumour-up log2FC 9.712 (padj 2.58e-30); protein log2FC 2.269. Open Targets score 0.3088. Tractable as antibody, small molecule and PROTAC (AB Advanced Clinical, SM Approved Drug). Drugs as returned: GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_3, IODINE I 124 GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_2, SULTHIAME PHASE_4, ETHOXZOLAMIDE WITHDRAWAL. UniProt: cell membrane and microvillus membrane, so it suits antibody/imaging use and is measurable as a tumour marker. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency (mean effect 0.051, selectivity 0.031), so it is a surface antigen and biomarker rather than an essential gene.

CD70 is rank 3 in convergence (score 4.2143). TCGA tumour-up log2FC 7.09 (padj 6.45e-25); protein log2FC 2.421. Open Targets score 0.0572, so the association is mainly literature. Tractability: AB and OC Advanced Clinical. Drugs as returned: CUSATUZUMAB PHASE_2, VORSETUZUMAB MAFODOTIN PHASE_1, VORSETUZUMAB PHASE_1, MDX-1411 PHASE_1. UniProt: cell membrane, so it is accessible to antibodies and ADCs. DepMap selectivity is 0.006 (not a dependency). This is an antigen-type target, not a lineage driver.

EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is an established ccRCC drug target. Open Targets score 0.4871 (genetic 0.5677, somatic 0.4559). Drug: BELZUTIFAN, APPROVAL. Tractability is small molecule (SM Approved Drug) plus PROTAC-type. DepMap is the only dependency signal among the top genes: ccRCC mean effect -0.143 versus 0.157 in other lines, selectivity 0.3, 0.208 of ccRCC lines dependent, padj 0.061, not common essential. Convergence rank 38; the tumour-vs-normal expression change is small (TCGA log2FC 0.461), so it is a target but not a differential-expression biomarker.

ENPP3 is rank 29 in convergence (score 3.2997). TCGA tumour-up log2FC 5.557 (padj 1.66e-22); protein log2FC 1.544. Open Targets score 0.0356, so the association is weak. Tractability: AB and OC (OC Advanced Clinical). Drug: AGS-16C3F, PHASE_2 (antibody-drug conjugate). UniProt: apical cell membrane and secreted. DepMap selectivity is 0.026, so there is no dependency. An ADC antigen candidate for ccRCC.

SLC16A3 (MCT4) is rank 15 in convergence (score 3.5532). TCGA tumour-up log2FC 3.291 (padj 7.66e-28); protein log2FC 2.279. Open Targets score 0.0491. Predicted tractable but no drug is listed. UniProt: lactate efflux transporter of the cell membrane, basolateral. No DepMap dependency (selectivity -0.008), so the target case is weak despite the glycolytic-phenotype rationale.

VHL is the ccRCC driver. Mutated in 247 of 511 tumours (frequency 0.483, padj 0.0, recurrent). Open Targets score 0.6466 (top association), somatic 0.814. Convergence rank 16 (score 3.5434), with 0.791 CNV-loss frequency. No drug is returned and it is a tumour suppressor, so it is not directly druggable. It is a mechanism and context gene; loss of VHL stabilises HIF-2alpha (EPAS1).

ALDOB is rank 2 in convergence (score 4.2206), a tumour-down biomarker. TCGA log2FC -4.741 (padj 6.57e-11); protein log2FC -2.273. Cox log HR -0.358 (padj 0.000023), so higher expression is associated with better survival. Open Targets score 0.0701. No drugs. Proximal-tubule loss marker with prognostic value, not a target.

SCARB1 is rank 5 in convergence (score 4.1052) and has the top target-profile score (4.1314) among these candidates. Open Targets score 0.4049 (genetic 0.519). TCGA tumour-up log2FC 3.989 (padj 1.43e-31); protein log2FC 1.837. Predicted tractable; no drug listed. DepMap selectivity is -0.021, so there is no dependency. Association is mostly genetic rather than direct ccRCC clinical evidence.

NNMT is rank 7 in convergence (score 3.9643) and has the best biomarker-profile score here (4.7744). TCGA tumour-up log2FC 4.685 (padj 5.62e-27); protein log2FC 2.709. Cox log HR 0.301 (padj 0.00479), so higher expression is associated with worse survival. Open Targets score 0.0598. No drug listed. DepMap mean effect 0.316 (not a dependency).

SLC22A8 (OAT3) is rank 4 in convergence (score 4.1667), a tumour-down transporter. TCGA log2FC -6.154 (padj 5.42e-13); protein log2FC -2.264. Cox log HR -0.402 (padj 0.0000433). Open Targets score 0.0662. Existing drugs for the family: PROBENECID PHASE_4, PRATOSARTAN PHASE_3. This is a loss biomarker; the drugs inhibit the transporter and are not useful for ccRCC, so it is not a therapeutic target.

caveats: Only CA9, SLC16A3, EPAS1 and VHL were checked directly with DepMap and mutation recurrence; for the other genes the DepMap values quoted come from the convergence ranking row. CA9 and SLC16A3 DepMap records returned evidence_id null and were not cited.

No candidate other than EPAS1 shows selective ccRCC dependency (DepMap), so antigen targets (CA9, CD70, ENPP3) rest on tumour-restricted surface expression and ADC/antibody rationale, not on gene essentiality.
Open Targets scores for most convergence-top genes are low (literature-driven); high Open Targets scores belong to driver genes (VHL, PBRM1, KDM5C, BAP1, SETD2) that are mostly not druggable.
STRING interactions were not queried; subcellular locations are from UniProt only for CA9, CD70, ENPP3 and SLC16A3.
Many top-ranked biomarkers are tumour-down proximal-tubule genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD) that may reflect normal-tissue contamination or lineage loss.

findings.statement: CA9 is tumor-cell intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.976 of tumor transcripts (54.7% of RCC cells express it) and the pure-tumour RNA log2FC extrapolated to purity 1 is 7.787, so the bulk signal (log2FC 6.312) is not stromal.
In paired tumor cell vs proximal tubule pseudobulk CA9 has log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189, 6 donors), and TCGA-KIRC replicates it (log2FC 9.712), supporting a tumor-vs-cell-of-origin biomarker.
In Visium, CA9 expression is assigned to RCC spots (composition-corrected share 0.999) and high spots are enriched for RCC neighbours (log2 enrichment 0.381, padj 0.0017), i.e. a tumor-cell niche.

CA9 best MGD site score is 0.546 (pocket 126.8 A3, pLDDT 90.3, 1 accessible lysine, model mean pLDDT 76.56); ligand-site recall is 0.5 but only 0.221 within top pockets. This ranks a site, not a glue; the pocket is small and likely the catalytic zinc site.

CD70 is up in ccRCC (TCGA log2FC 7.09) and survives purity extrapolation (RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 4.278), consistent with tumor-intrinsic expression; clinical-stage antibodies exist (vorsetuzumab, cusatuzumab, up to phase 2). Single-cell shows some T/B-cell expression, so an off-tumor immune caveat applies.

NNMT is tumor-cell intrinsic: the RNA log2FC at purity 1 is 5.256 (bulk RNA log2FC 4.67, protein 2.709) and TCGA log2FC is 4.685, with adverse prognosis (Cox log HR 0.301); no clinical drug is listed.

KDR is an endothelial gene, not a tumor-cell target: endothelium holds 0.951 of tumor transcripts (40.5% of endothelial cells express it) and Visium shows endothelial composition-corrected share 0.99 versus 0.002 for RCC.

CD74 transcripts are immune: macrophages hold 0.436 and CD8 T cells 0.345 of tumor transcripts (cDC 0.114), and Visium assigns a composition-corrected share of 0.637 to macrophages, so the bulk signal is infiltrating immune cells, not tumor cells.
CXCR4 is expressed by lymphocytes: CD8 T cells hold 0.563 of tumor transcripts and CD4 T cells have the highest expressing fraction (87.8%), so it is an immune microenvironment target.
MET is mostly tumor-cell expressed: RCC cells hold 0.935 of tumor transcripts but only 35.2% of RCC cells express it (cpm_share 0.682); endothelium has 12% expressing cells.

EPAS1 transcripts in tumor are mostly non-tumor: endothelium holds 0.365 and fibroblasts 0.081 of transcripts, RCC cells only 0.051 (4.9% expressing), so EPAS1 is not a clean tumor-cell expression marker in this dataset.

COL23A1 is the top tumor-track first-in-class candidate: RCC cells hold 0.881 of tumor transcripts, 7 ccRCC papers, no clinical drug, AB/PR tractable, surface/secreted, max vital-organ nTPM 3 (heart muscle), TCGA log2FC 5.829, log2FC at purity 1 of 4.88. Hypothesis only: no dependency evidence (DepMap mean effect 0.167, not selective); literature counted by gene symbol. AlphaFold model is poor (mean pLDDT 58.91; best MGD site 0.2342, 8.0 A3), so not a glue candidate.

RAB42 is a second tumor-track candidate: RCC cells hold 0.627 of tumor transcripts, 2 ccRCC papers (20 total), no clinical drug, TCGA log2FC 4.371 and log2FC at purity 1 of 3.189; vital-organ max 2.6 nTPM (lung). Best MGD site is 0.5348 (37.4 A3, 3 accessible lysines, model pLDDT 85.31) with no ligand-site validation. Hypothesis; no functional or dependency evidence.

OLFML2A is a stroma-track candidate carried by fibroblasts (0.647 of tumor transcripts), 2 ccRCC papers, no clinical drug, antibody-tractable; TCGA log2FC 2.372, log2FC at purity 1 of 1.527. Vital-organ max 27.9 nTPM (colon) is an off-tumor caveat, and it targets the microenvironment rather than tumor cells. Hypothesis only.

JAG2 is an endothelial stroma-track candidate (0.487 of tumor transcripts), 9 ccRCC papers, no clinical drug, antibody-tractable; TCGA log2FC 1.549, log2FC at purity 1 of 1.061, TCGA survival layer present; vital-organ max 12.7 nTPM (heart muscle). Hypothesis; DepMap mean effect 0.204, not a selective dependency.

SLC37A2 is a macrophage immune-track candidate (0.886 of tumor transcripts), 2 ccRCC papers, no clinical drug, AB/PR tractable; TCGA log2FC 3.093 and log2FC at purity 1 of 0.619 (purity robust). Best MGD site 0.7403 (228.1 A3, depth 11.79, 4 accessible lysines, model pLDDT 83.94), ligand-site recall 1.0 from a single ligand. Immune-cell target; hypothesis only.

LILRB4 is flagged infiltration-driven: macrophages hold 0.933 of tumor transcripts, TCGA log2FC 3.7 but log2FC at purity 1 only 0.508 (not purity-robust), so its bulk up-regulation reflects immune infiltration rather than tumor-cell expression.

caveats: Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses: concordant tumor-up expression does not show functional requirement; literature counts are by gene symbol; DepMap shows no selective dependency for the quoted genes.
MGD scores rank pockets only and do not imply a glue exists; several pockets are small (<130 A3) or have low-confidence models, and ligand-site recall from few ligands is weak evidence.

CD70 and NNMT single-cell and tumor-vs-PT values returned without evidence ids, so they are not quoted; their tumor-intrinsic claim rests on purity-extrapolated bulk data. Convergence top ranks ALDOB, SLC22A8, PIGR, UMOD, FABP1 are down in tumor (normal-tubule markers) and were not profiled at single-cell level.
EGFR was not profiled within the tool budget; tumour-cell scRNA has only one PT donor (39 cells) in some comparisons.

summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the strongest and most robust convergent evidence. It leads the overall convergence ranking (score 4.5197) and is the only gene that stays in the overall top ten under random re-weighting (p_top10 0.894). It is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712), survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 7.787), and single-cell data place 0.976 of its tumour transcripts in RCC cells. Girentuximab reached PHASE_3. DepMap shows no dependency (mean effect 0.051), so CA9 is an antibody, imaging and diagnostic target rather than an essential gene.

A second tier of tumour-up candidates is protein-confirmed, replicated in TCGA-KIRC and purity-robust: SCARB1 (top of the target profile), CD70, NNMT, SLC16A3 (MCT4) and ENPP3. CD70 and ENPP3 already have antibody or ADC programmes. NNMT adds adverse prognosis and supportive ccRCC literature. SCARB1 has no ccRCC literature relations in the corpus, which makes it the most novel of the group. None of these genes is a selective DepMap dependency, so the target calls rest on tumour-restricted expression and tractability, not on essentiality.

The biomarker profile is led by genes lost with proximal-tubule identity: PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, SLC6A19 and PPP1R1A, together with ALDOB and SLC22A8 in the overall ranking. They are down in tumour at RNA and protein, replicate in TCGA-KIRC and carry significant TCGA survival associations. They are diagnostic and prognostic candidates, not therapeutic targets.

The clinically validated ccRCC axes appear as context, not as data-led discoveries. VHL is the dominant somatic driver, EPAS1 (belzutifan, approved) is the only candidate with ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency, and KDR is an endothelial angiogenesis target. Discovery candidates (COL23A1 and RAB42 in tumour, OLFML2A and JAG2 in stroma, SLC37A2 and LILRB4 in the immune track) are data-ranked hypotheses without dependency evidence.

omics.text: In CPTAC tumour-vs-normal data CA9 is the clearest up-regulated candidate: RNA log2FC 6.312 and protein log2FC 2.269, with a modest positive copy-number cis effect (rho 0.224).

Other tumour-up genes with protein confirmation are SCARB1 (RNA log2FC 2.974, protein 1.837), CD70 (RNA 4.464, protein 2.421), NNMT (RNA 4.67, protein 2.709), SLC16A3 (RNA 3.435, protein 2.279) and ENPP3 (RNA 3.895, protein 1.544).
FABP6 is up at RNA (log2FC 4.006) and protein (log2FC 1.921), and its copy number is gained in 0.573 of tumours with a cis effect of rho 0.309, a plausible dosage contribution.
On the loss side, ALDH6A1 is down at RNA (log2FC -3.399) and protein (log2FC -1.925), with CNV loss frequency 0.355 and a positive cis effect (rho 0.525), consistent with a copy-loss dosage effect.

literature.text: Literature support is concentrated on CA9, CD70 and NNMT. CA9-targeted PET is described as proof-of-concept warranting prospective validation. CD70 is reported as overexpressed in RCC with minimal normal-tissue expression, as a downstream HIF target, and as the subject of 68Ga-labelled single-domain-antibody tracers. NNMT is described as a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target, and selective tool inhibitors exist in a non-ccRCC chemistry paper.

Biomarker literature for the down-regulated genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, ABAT) rests mostly on single bioinformatic or IHC studies. UMOD loss is the most reproduced across independent studies. The corpus has a contradiction for MT1G, which is low in tumour yet linked to poor prognosis when high. FABP1 relations concern colorectal and lung cancer rather than ccRCC, and SCARB1 has no extracted ccRCC literature relations despite strong data support.

external.text: Open Targets drug records separate candidates with clinical programmes from untested ones. CA9 (girentuximab, PHASE_3), CD70 (cusatuzumab, PHASE_2) and ENPP3 (AGS-16C3F, PHASE_2) are membrane proteins accessible to antibodies or ADCs. NNMT, SCARB1 and SLC16A3 have predicted tractability only and no drugs listed.

EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the established ccRCC target with belzutifan approved. DepMap shows a selective but partial dependency (selectivity 0.3, fraction of ccRCC lines dependent 0.208, padj 0.061), and it is not common essential.
VHL is the core driver, mutated in 247 of 511 tumours (frequency 0.483). It has no drug of its own, so the therapeutic route runs through HIF-2alpha downstream.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-cell intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.976 of its tumour transcripts (54.7% of RCC cells express it), and tumour cells versus proximal tubule give log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189).

Several clinical candidates are microenvironmental rather than tumour-intrinsic. KDR is endothelial (0.951 of transcripts), CD74 is carried mainly by macrophages (0.436), and CXCR4 by CD8 T cells (0.563). EPAS1 transcripts in this scRNA-seq dataset are mostly endothelial (0.365) rather than RCC (0.051). By contrast MET is mainly tumour-cell (0.935). CD70 and NNMT single-cell records carried no evidence ids, so their cell-level split is not quoted; their purity-1 log2FC values support tumour-intrinsic expression, and CD70 has some T/B-cell expression, an off-tumour caveat.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, CA9 expression is assigned to RCC spots (composition-corrected share 0.999), and high-CA9 spots are enriched for RCC neighbours (log2 enrichment 0.381, padj 0.0017). CA9 therefore marks tumour-cell-rich niches.

The microenvironment genes look the same in situ. KDR spots are explained by endothelium (composition-corrected share 0.99, RCC 0.002), and CD74 spots mostly by macrophages (0.637), so their bulk signals come from vessels and immune infiltrate, not tumour cells.

structure.text: Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank candidate sites; they are not evidence that a degrader exists. CA9's best site scores 0.546 (volume 126.8 A3, pocket pLDDT 90.3, one accessible lysine), with ligand-site recall 0.5. The pocket is small and probably the catalytic zinc site, a modest site for a protein already addressed by antibodies.

Among discovery candidates, SLC37A2 has the highest-ranked site (score 0.7403, volume 228.1 A3, 4 accessible lysines, model pLDDT 83.94), with ligand-site recall 1.0 from a single ligand, which is weak support. SLC37A2 is a macrophage protein, so a degrader there would act on immune cells, not tumour cells.
RAB42, a tumour-track candidate, has the next-best site (score 0.5348, mean pLDDT 85.31, 3 accessible lysines), but the pocket is small (37.4 A3) and lacks ligand validation.
The COL23A1 model is poor (mean pLDDT 58.91) with a single 8.0 A3 pocket scoring 0.2342, so it is not a credible degrader site.

discovery.text: The tumour-track discovery lead is COL23A1. It is novel in having no clinical drug, and it is antibody or PROTAC tractable, surface or secreted, with low vital-organ expression (3 nTPM, heart muscle). RCC cells carry 0.881 of its transcripts. It replicates in TCGA (log2FC 5.829) and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (log2FC at purity 1 of 4.88). It shows no dependency (DepMap mean effect 0.167).

RAB42 is a second tumour-track hypothesis: RCC cells hold 0.627 of its transcripts, there is no clinical drug, vital-organ expression peaks at 2.6 nTPM (lung), and it replicates in TCGA (log2FC 4.371) with a purity-1 log2FC of 3.189. There is no functional or dependency evidence.

The stroma track gives OLFML2A (fibroblast-borne, 0.647 of transcripts; TCGA log2FC 2.372, purity-1 log2FC 1.527; vital-organ expression 27.9 nTPM in colon) and JAG2 (mostly endothelial, 0.487; TCGA log2FC 1.549, purity-1 log2FC 1.061; DepMap mean effect 0.204). Both target the microenvironment, have modest effect sizes and lack functional evidence.

The immune track is mostly infiltration. SLC37A2 is macrophage-borne (0.886) with TCGA log2FC 3.093 that shrinks to 0.619 at purity 1, and LILRB4 (macrophage, 0.933) has TCGA log2FC 3.7 that falls to 0.508 at purity 1. Both bulk signals largely reflect macrophage abundance, so these are immune-cell targets at best. All discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; none is a selective dependency.

validation.text: External replication in TCGA-KIRC is strong for the leading targets: CA9 (log2FC 9.712), CD70 (7.09), ENPP3 (5.557), NNMT (4.685), SCARB1 (3.989) and SLC16A3 (3.291). All stay up when extrapolated to a pure tumour (purity-1 RNA log2FC 7.787, 4.278, 5.278, 5.256, 3.762 and 3.821), so these changes come from tumour cells rather than infiltration.

Prognosis strengthens NNMT: higher expression is adverse in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479). DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency for NNMT (mean effect 0.316), which weakens its case as a functional target.

The independent layers weaken the essentiality case across the board. None of the top candidates is a recurrent somatic driver (VHL is, at frequency 0.483, and PBRM1 at 0.362), and EPAS1 is the only selective DepMap dependency (selectivity 0.3). On the biomarker side ALDH6A1 is weakened by the purity check, since its RNA change shrinks from -3.399 to -1.973 at purity 1, while PSAT1 keeps most of it.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting, the target profile is stable at the top. SCARB1 (p_top10 0.968, rank interval 1 to 8), CA9 (0.941, 1 to 13), SLC16A3 (0.881), CD70 and NNMT (0.88 each), ENPP3 (0.823) and FABP6 (0.803) form the robust target top ten. In the biomarker profile PSAT1 is the most stable call (p_top10 0.986, rank interval 1 to 4), followed by PCK1 (0.889), SLC6A19 (0.881) and PPP1R1A (0.8).

Other positions depend on the chosen weights. In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 is robustly top ten (p_top10 0.894). In the biomarker profile, DUSP9 (p_top10 0.398, with a 90% rank interval reaching 117) and SLPI (p_top10 0.333) are fragile, as are target-profile entries from rank 11 down, such as PNCK (p_top10 0.004).

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most fully on CA9 and CD70: both are tumour-intrinsic, protein-confirmed, TCGA-replicated, literature-backed and clinically addressed. NNMT converges on omics, literature and prognosis but lacks a drug. SCARB1, ENPP3 and SLC16A3 are data-led, with thin or absent ccRCC literature.

The disagreements are informative. The validated clinical axes (VHL, EPAS1) score high in Open Targets but not in the omics convergence, and EPAS1 transcripts are mostly non-tumour in single-cell data. Down-regulated tubule-identity genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, PSAT1) top the overall and biomarker rankings but are biomarkers, not targets, and literature calling ALDOB a potential target is not supported by its data-only target profile.

limitations.text: No leading candidate is a selective DepMap dependency; target calls rest on tumour-restricted expression, replication and tractability, not on essentiality.
The biomarker ranking is dominated by proximal-tubule genes whose tumour-vs-normal loss partly reflects cell-of-origin differences; prognosis is univariate Cox in TCGA-KIRC only.
Literature support for most genes comes from single bioinformatic or small IHC studies; CA9 and CD70 translational work is early-stage.
Single-cell records for CD70 and NNMT returned without evidence ids, so their cell-type split is not quoted; down-regulated convergence genes were not profiled at single-cell level.
Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank AlphaFold pockets and do not indicate that a degrader exists.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; literature counts are by gene symbol and immune-track genes are largely infiltration-driven.

targets.rationale: Strongest convergence overall and second in the target profile (p_top10 0.941): tumour-intrinsic (0.976 of transcripts in RCC cells, purity-1 log2FC 7.787), TCGA-replicated (log2FC 9.712), literature-backed and addressed by girentuximab (PHASE_3). No DepMap dependency, so it is an antibody, imaging and diagnostic target.

Tumour-up at RNA (log2FC 4.464) and protein (log2FC 2.421), TCGA-replicated (log2FC 7.09), purity-robust (4.278), membrane-located with clinical antibodies (cusatuzumab PHASE_2) and supporting ccRCC literature. Ranked above SCARB1 despite a lower target-profile score because the literature and drug layers add independent support; some T/B-cell expression is an off-tumour caveat.

Top of the target profile (score 4.1314, p_top10 0.968): tumour-up (RNA log2FC 2.974, protein 1.837), TCGA-replicated (log2FC 3.989), purity-robust (3.762) and genetically associated in Open Targets (0.519). No drug, no ccRCC literature and no dependency, so it is the leading novel target hypothesis.

Tumour-intrinsic and protein-confirmed (RNA log2FC 4.67, protein 2.709, purity-1 5.256), TCGA-replicated (4.685), adverse prognosis (Cox log HR 0.301) and literature support as prognostic marker. No clinical drug and no dependency (mean effect 0.316), so the biomarker call is firmer than the target call.

Tumour-up (RNA log2FC 3.895, protein 1.544), TCGA-replicated (5.557), purity-robust (5.278), apical membrane protein with an ADC (AGS-16C3F, PHASE_2). Robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.823) but has thin ccRCC literature in the corpus.

MCT4 lactate transporter, tumour-up (RNA log2FC 3.435, protein 2.279), TCGA-replicated (3.291), purity-robust (3.821) and stable in the target profile (p_top10 0.881). Predicted tractable but undrugged and not a dependency.
The most robust biomarker call (biomarker score 5.3696, p_top10 0.986): down at RNA (log2FC -3.867) and protein (-1.963), TCGA-replicated (-2.974) and prognostic (Cox log HR 0.43, padj 5.66e-7).

Loss of proximal-tubule gluconeogenic identity: down at RNA (log2FC -4.424) and protein (-1.859), TCGA-replicated (-3.079) and prognostic (Cox log HR -0.415, padj 1.91e-7); stable in the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.889).

Second in overall convergence: down in TCGA (log2FC -4.741), down at protein (-2.273), favourable when high (Cox log HR -0.358) and supported by ccRCC prognostic literature. A lost-expression gene, so not a target.

Strongest prognostic association among the biomarkers (Cox log HR -0.554, padj 9.45e-12) with a copy-loss dosage effect (cis rho 0.525). Placed below PSAT1 and PCK1 because its rank interval is wider (rank_p95 33) and its RNA change shrinks to -1.973 at purity 1.

Not a convergence-led candidate, but the only selective ccRCC DepMap dependency (selectivity 0.3) and the approved belzutifan target. Kept as the clinical benchmark; its transcripts are mostly non-tumour in scRNA-seq (RCC 0.051).
